findings.title: Reminder cancellation is never awaited
findings.body: The new cancel path calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach and never awaits those promises (they are also no longer included in the Promise.all that used to wait for reminder DB writes). deleteScheduledEmailReminder only persists cancelled=true (or deletes the row) inside that promise. On a Next.js/serverless handler the process can freeze as soon as the response is returned, so the flag is often never written and the cron never sees the reminder. The same un-awaited forEach is used in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx (requestReschedule, around line 488) and packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx (disabled event types / edited steps). Cancelled and rescheduled bookings will keep sending workflow emails.

findings.title: Past cancelled reminders are deleted before SendGrid cancel
findings.body: The cron first deleteMany's every EMAIL WorkflowReminder whose scheduledDate is already <= now, including rows with cancelled=true, and only afterwards looks up cancelled reminders to POST a SendGrid batch cancel. Any cancelled reminder whose send time has passed (cron delayed, or the 15-minute job running after a reminder that was inside the one-hour window) is removed from the database without ever calling /v3/user/scheduled_sends. SendGrid still has the batch and delivers the email, and there is no row left to retry. Cancellation must run before that delete, and past cancelled rows must not be removed until the batch cancel succeeds.

findings.title: immediateDelete reintroduces the 100-cancel cap and skips retry
findings.body: When immediateDelete is true (reschedule in handleNewBooking.ts, workflow delete, and deleted workflow steps), the function POSTs status=cancel to SendGrid and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. That is the same immediate scheduled_sends cancel the PR says fails once 100 cancellations are pending. The error is only console.logged, cancelled stays null, so the cron will not retry, and the email is still sent. Reschedule — one of the two cases this PR claims to fix — always takes this path. immediateDelete also does not remove the DB row, so a failed cancel cannot be recovered later.

findings.title: One SendGrid error aborts every pending cancel
findings.body: Cancellation is a single try around the whole for-loop, and prisma.workflowReminder.delete promises are only executed in Promise.all after every SendGrid call succeeds. If any request throws (null referenceId, already-cancelled batch, rate limit, one bad batch_id), the catch logs and exits: remaining reminders are not cancelled, and deletes for batches that were already cancelled in SendGrid never run. On the next cron those already-cancelled batches are retried first, fail again, and block every later reminder indefinitely. Each reminder needs its own try/catch, and the DB row should be deleted only after that reminder's cancel succeeds. The query also does not restrict method to EMAIL or require a non-null referenceId, so an SMS sid or null batch_id can poison the loop.

findings.title: Paid cancellation returns before reminders are cancelled
findings.body: When bookingToDelete.paid is set, the handler refunds, marks the booking REJECTED, awaits apiDeletes, and returns at the 'Booking successfully cancelled' path. The workflow-reminder cancellation added below that return (the forEach over updatedBookings.workflowReminders) never runs for paid bookings. Those bookings still have scheduled SendGrid/Twilio reminders, so cancelling a paid booking continues to send workflow emails.
